Kevin (AE): Quick sync — Olivia's infra team wants to freeze upgrades for the on‑prem POC for up to 9 months. They also want a formal rollback SLA exemption and a documented emergency hotfix path. Is that feasible?
Maya (SE): Short answer: yes, with caveats. We can do a freeze for POC but need an emergency path for critical security fixes.
Olivia (Customer): Correct — we can't accept automatic updates. If there's a security fix, we want a signed hotfix delivered via our approved channel (sneakernet or scp to an airgapped jumpbox).
Maya (SE): Understood. Operationally we can produce signed delta bundles + signed manifest. Customer verifies signatures + checksums before install. Example verification: `sha256sum redwood-bundle-v1.2.3.tar.gz && cat manifest.json | jq .sha256`
Toni (GTM): Any commercial impact? If we produce manual signed hotfixes and keep images frozen that sounds like additional ops/PS work.
Maya (SE): Yes — two lines of effort: 1) Bundle/signing + manual packaging per hotfix; 2) Offline delivery coordination (HSM/KMS export, Notary signing ops). Recommend a fixed PS bucket for freeze+hotfix support.
Kevin (AE): Olivia — would you accept a contract that includes a quarterly security review plus paid emergency hotfix credits?
Olivia (Customer): We prefer predefined SLAs for emergency response (e.g., 48h turnaround for critical patches) rather than ad‑hoc credit requests.
Maya (SE): 48h for producing a signed hotfix artifact is tight but doable if we pre-stage keys and have a small oncall rotation. We need: signed manifest, signed image, instructions, and checksum. We also need a signed attestation from our Notary service stating signature provenance.
Kevin (AE): Any blocking technical constraints for long freeze? What about model bundle drift or license/third‑party deps?
Maya (SE): Biggest risks: 1) Transitive dependency vulns in bundled libs; 2) Model file format incompatibilities if customers later upgrade runtime; 3) Drift in hardware drivers (GPU/accelerator) over 9 months. We'll document compatibility matrix and lock recommended runtime image.
Maya (SE): Also: signed delta bundles are smaller, but if model weights change significantly we may need full-image releases. We can limit scope: freeze applies to platform + model version X only.
Toni (GTM): Commercial proposal: include a "Freeze + Hotfix" SOW line item: up to N emergency hotfixes per year, 48–72h SLA for critical, separate line for out-of-scope work. Pricing impact ~ 20–30% uplift on Dedicated POC support.
Olivia (Customer): That sounds reasonable. We can't do cloud callbacks, so delivery via USB or customer-provisioned jumpbox is acceptable. We need MD5/sha verification instructions and a chain-of-custody manifest.
Maya (SE): We'll add chain-of-custody template: timestamped manifest, signer CN, signature, and `sha256`. For sneakernet we recommend using signed manifests + tamper-evident packaging.
Kevin (AE): Next actions: Maya draft technical runbook + verification commands; Toni draft SOW language and pricing; Olivia to confirm acceptance of 48h SLA and delivery channel.
deploy-bot: Ticket SLS-2791 created (freeze-hotfix-runbook).
Olivia (Customer): ETA: I'll confirm internally by EOD Thu. Thanks for the quick replies. :thumbsup:
Maya (SE): I'll drop a short runbook in this thread with the exact commands and the manifest template once SLS-2791 is owned.
Kevin (AE): Thanks all — if the customer signs the freeze we'll spin up a PS kickoff and a one-hour runbook handoff session.
Olivia (Customer): Please include our security contact (sec-ops@olivia-corp.com) in the runbook handoff.
Maya (SE): Will do.
Toni (GTM): I'll prepare the SOW draft and send a version for review tomorrow.
Kevin (AE): Closing loop — will update when Olivia confirms.
